title: The Facts Are True, the News Is Fake
coreMove: Separate the raw event from the selection, salience, and frame that made it feel like the whole reality.
sourcePressure: A narrative can distort judgment while each selected fact remains technically true.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the chapter into generic media outrage or claims that facts do not matter.

sourceAnchors.name: The Facts Are True, the News Is Fake
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen title and sidecar support the distinction between true facts and misleading narrative packaging.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The useful tension is that the fact may be true and still leave the reader with a false map of what matters.

hook: opening with a tidy definition of skin in the game
starting with a generic meeting room where someone learns accountability
using a macho risk-taking cold open
counterintuition: not just X but Y correction shell
most people think fairness means niceness
the obvious lesson is wrong because the real lesson is deeper
tryThisNow: set a timer and think about risk
write down three ways to be accountable
ask yourself who has skin in the game with no concrete object

kitchen-table family advice with a mug
abstract consultant conversation with no downside transfer

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: local newsroom selecting one crime clip that skews neighborhood risk
exampleSpecs.audience: editor separating true fact from false map
exampleSpecs.stakes: residents may misjudge danger because salience has been engineered
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Manon places the clip beside the month's incident table before approving the homepage lead.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a police scanner beside a spreadsheet

exampleSpecs.domain: investor reading a true but cherry-picked market story
exampleSpecs.audience: portfolio manager detecting narrative packaging around facts
exampleSpecs.stakes: clients may sell on a story that hides base context
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lars asks what true facts were left out before forwarding the market note.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a market note printed beside a return chart

exampleSpecs.domain: school parent group reacting to a viral hallway video
exampleSpecs.audience: principal restoring sequence around a true clip
exampleSpecs.stakes: a student could be judged by a fragment without the surrounding event
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Paula lines up the timestamped hallway footage before drafting the parent letter.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: locker doors flashing in paused video

exampleSpecs.domain: public-health dashboard headline missing denominator context
exampleSpecs.audience: analyst preventing true numbers from becoming false urgency
exampleSpecs.stakes: resource allocation could follow panic rather than risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Jack adds denominators and trend lines before the alert leaves the dashboard.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: amber cells on a dashboard screen

exampleSpecs.domain: sports article praising a player from one highlight while hiding defensive errors
exampleSpecs.audience: coach teaching athletes to resist packaged salience
exampleSpecs.stakes: training choices may chase clips instead of performance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Min pauses the highlight reel and adds the missed rotations back into the review.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sneakers squeaking under a projector hum

exampleSpecs.domain: tenant association interpreting a landlord email without maintenance records
exampleSpecs.stakes: neighbors may accept a rent story that omits repair history
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aleksy pins the email next to the maintenance log and asks what story survives both.
